_notes: THE TUNING DIALS. Every number here was a `const` in a .gd file until
2026-08-05. They are decisions a DESIGNER makes, not structure a
programmer owns, so they live in data where a balance pass can move them
without touching a program, and where tests/simulate.gd can read the same
values the game runs on.
What belongs here: costs, caps, limits, rates, the starting kit, prices.
What does NOT: layout geometry (that is a per-screen zone template, law
12), file paths, type names, and anything the engine's structure depends
on. If changing the number can only ever break the build rather than
change the game, it is not a dial.
Every key here has a matching default in core/rules.gd. A missing key
falls back to that default rather than crashing, so a half-written file
degrades to the shipped balance instead of to a black screen. Catalog
validation checks the values are sane; tests/unit/test_rules.gd checks
that this file and the defaults still agree on the shipped numbers.
The hand is the shape of a turn; paws are how much you may DO in one.
Spent energy never reshuffles (owner rule, load-bearing) -- that is
structure, not a dial, and has no key here on purpose. Banking was
removed 2026-08-08 (owner: a saved card was just a stolen card waiting).
How Ash enters a fight. Prices are FLAT -- the environment's cost_mod
deliberately does not touch them (owner rule 2026-08-03): how you go in
is about you, not about the alley. A discount here once made the
chooser quote a price the player could not predict.
Display names live in story/interface.json under battle.approach.* --
what an approach COSTS is a rule, what it READS like is writing.
The wager. press_on_mult is how much richer each fight deeper makes
the satchel; slip_forfeit is what going over the wall in a hurry
spills; toll_rate is the Hollow Court's cut of banked gleam on a death
after the first.
Level-1 Ash (owner calibration 2026-08-01): 10 HP, and a starter deck
of 15 cards that are ALL value 1 -- potent 2s and 3s are rewards, not
starting kit (owner rarity rule). Growth arrives as the residue of
difficult work; there is no XP bar and no level number in the game.
prologue_skills is what a finished prologue IMPLIES for a save that
predates progressive unlocks (law 7).
The Magpie Exchange. What each good COSTS is a rule; what it is CALLED
is writing and lives in story/interface.json keyed by mode (law 20).
deck_floor is the thinnest spool the loadout's re-spool editor allows
(owner 2026-08-08: cutting is free selection at home, not a purchase)
-- an unbounded thinner turns the spool from a fuel gauge into a combo.
tonic_hp is what one tonic adds to Ash's lives.
Shared module dials. crossing.night_presses_turn is when The Long Way
Round stops being patient with you.
Numbers the WRITING depends on. recap_line_max is a text budget, not a
style choice: a lead's recap line shares one story page with two other
lines and a fixed illustration, and the story screen silently retires
whatever overflows -- so an over-long line does not look like a bug, it
looks like a missing line. flashback_tint is the one sepia every
Remembered Day uses, so memory reads the same everywhere.
